meta.title: Conflict Watchlist
meta.reviewer: CSI analyst review, 23 Sep 2026 (briefed theatres from the weekly brief through 21 Sep; other theatres web-researched — items marked unverified need confirmation)
meta.notes: Analyst-maintained register. Each review: (1) set reviewDate/previousReviewDate, (2) for every item move `prev` <- `now` on the five dimensions and then set the new `now`, (3) rewrite `changes`, `next` and `csi` for what is true THIS week only, (4) record any state move in `history`. The dashboard derives attention rank, movements, changed-dimension flags, staleness and the brief signal — do not type those in. This is a watchlist, not a news archive: keep `changes` to what materially moved since the previous review, and `next` to named, checkable indicators.

1.name: Priority Conflicts
1.desc: High relevance to the Army — followed every week in the brief.

2.name: Active Regional & Escalation Watches
2.desc: Regional theatres where escalation would change Singapore's or the Army's picture.

3.name: Baseline Regional Research Reserve
3.desc: Held for pattern and case-study value; reviewed on trigger or on the monthly cycle.

Priority.desc: Direct strategic relevance or high Army learning value.

Active.desc: Material trend, escalation, or regional relevance.

Watch.desc: Baseline monitoring; no current learning priority.

Archive.desc: Reserve — retained for reference and pattern work; revisit only on a named trigger.

CSI Flash.desc: Same-day short note: a threshold was crossed or Singapore exposure changed.

Weekly awareness post.desc: One item in this week's brief or awareness post.

Monthly pattern review.desc: Feed the monthly tactical-learning / pattern cycle.

Quarterly candidate.desc: Candidate for a quarterly deep-dive or case study.

attentionScore.desc: Deterministic, explainable rank. state (Priority 40 / Active 25 / Watch 10 / Archive 0) + escalation risk (Severe 20 / High 15 / Moderate 8 / Low 2) + 5 per dimension that changed since the previous review + 10 if the state moved up + CSI action (Flash 20 / Weekly 10 / Monthly 5 / Quarterly 3 / Dashboard 0) + Singapore exposure (High 8 / Moderate 4 / Low 0) + tier (T1 6 / T2 3 / T3 0). Items flagged ignore-for-now are shown but ranked last.

items.name: Russia–Ukraine

phase.now: Attritional war with reciprocal deep-strike campaigns

items.whyNow: Richest adaptation feed on the list: Russia's shift to jet-powered Geran-4/5 strike packages, Ukraine's 3,000 km strike on Yamal gas plants and Operation Vivaldi at Lyman — while a live talks track (UNGA meetings, an October trilateral) could change the frame.
changes: Russia's strike architecture shifted to jet-powered drones: Geran-4/5 were ~56% of long-range drone strikes in August (total volume down from 6,583 in April to 4,943), exploiting Ukraine's anti-ballistic interceptor deficit; MoD warned on 31 Aug of 'massive strikes' on energy sites before winter.

Ukraine's deep-strike campaign hit the Syzran, NORSI and Kirishi refineries (23–30 Aug) and on 9 Sep the Novy Urengoy and Purovsky gas-condensate plants 3,000 km inside Russia; Russia suspended gasoline exports to 30 Sep.

Operation Vivaldi (from mid-Sep) reduced the Lyman salient (85–125 km² claimed, Russians pushed back across the Chornyi Zherebets) under Maj Gen Drapatyi's decentralised, drone-first C2 after the July leadership reshuffle in Kyiv.

Diplomacy re-opened without a breakthrough: US envoys in Kyiv and Moscow (early Sep), BRICS (India, China) offered mediation, Trump–Zelensky met at UNGA on 22 Sep and Rubio–Lavrov on 23 Sep; Ukraine is pushing an energy-infrastructure and Black Sea truce.
Russian drone incursions into Polish and Romanian airspace drew a NATO condemnation on 12 Aug; Romania reports spill-over rising 'exponentially'.

next.text: Next US–Ukraine–Russia trilateral round (Budanov: 'for October'; UAE venue proposed) and the Ukraine–US–Europe follow-up.
next.ifSeen: Energy or Black Sea truce terms on the table → Weekly awareness post; watch for a strike pause as a bargaining signal.

next.text: Opening of Russia's 2026–27 winter energy campaign: mass Geran-4/5 plus ballistic packages against generation and heating.
next.ifSeen: Weekly awareness post on saturation volume versus interceptor stocks.

next.text: European Council, Brussels: Ukraine's €23bn 2026 financing gap and the reparations loan on frozen assets (Belgian veto risk).
next.ifSeen: Financing settled → sustainment picture stable through winter; failure → note for the monthly review.

next.text: EU 21st sanctions package: wind-down for pre-24 July contracts ends; Commission review of refinery designations.
next.ifSeen: Tightening confirmed → sustainment pressure on Russian refining compounds Ukrainian strikes.

next.text: Vivaldi phase 2 or a Russian counter-concentration south-west of Kramatorsk (Druzhkivka, Dobropillia) and around Orikhiv.
next.ifSeen: Phase check: attritional gridlock versus an operational-level shift.

next.text: G20 Leaders' Summit, Miami — Zelensky says he is ready to meet Putin there if Putin attends.
next.ifSeen: A leaders' meeting would reset the diplomatic phase → CSI Flash.

csi.rationale: Jet-drone transition, production-chain and 3,000 km deep strikes are directly transferable to GBAD and installation-protection planning; volume-saturation fires versus interceptor economics stays the quarterly candidate.

items.name: Israel–Palestine (Gaza)

phase.now: Counter-insurgency behind the Yellow Line; Phase 2 stalled

items.whyNow: The feared return to large-scale operations did not happen; the phase settled into low-signature counter-insurgency behind a Yellow Line at ~70% of Gaza. The learning is in targeting of force-regeneration enablers and a SOF capture raid; the October ISF pilot deployment is the next real test.
changes: IDF holds ~70% of Gaza behind 'Yellow Line' earthworks; Netanyahu: 'We are not withdrawing. We are staying on this line.' Board of Peace 15-point roadmap (30 Jul) accepted by Hamas, rejected by Netanyahu on 9 Aug (full disarmament before withdrawal); no timetable clock has started.

Israeli cabinet approved a ~200-troop International Stabilisation Force pilot near Rafah (26 Jul); Uganda's parliament approved 1,200 troops for an October deployment, Morocco and Burundi in frame — but October is reported 'in doubt'.

Operational method shifted to precision attrition of Hamas's force-regeneration network (Khan Younis brigade commander al-Yazouri, engineering and IED specialists) and a special-operations capture raid in Gaza City (internal-security chief al-Arabeed, early Sep).

Escalation risk lowered from High to Moderate: pressure is applied by strikes on dual-use and utility sites (24 Aug desalination plant), evacuation orders and incendiary or unconventional reconnaissance rather than ground manoeuvre.

next.text: Ugandan (~1,200) and Moroccan ISF contingents enter the Rafah test zone (planned for October; reported in doubt).
next.ifSeen: First third-party force in Gaza → Monthly pattern review on stabilisation-force entry; slippage → Board of Peace credibility falls.

next.text: Israeli approval of the Board of Peace roadmap, starting the 14-day timetable and the 8-month disarmament clock.
next.ifSeen: Phase change to managed transition → Weekly awareness post.

next.text: Israeli Knesset election — drives Netanyahu's Gaza sequencing stance until results are confirmed on 4 Nov.
next.ifSeen: Re-check phase and CSI action after the result.

next.text: Yellow Line pushed beyond ~70% or the first 'Green Rafah' housing caravans permitted (earliest November).
next.ifSeen: Low-signature territorial consolidation pattern for the monthly review.

next.text: Return of large-scale ground operations, or a Hamas mass-casualty attack on IDF positions along the line.
next.ifSeen: Move to Priority; CSI Flash on phase change.

csi.rationale: High-payoff targeting of technical enablers and the Gaza City capture raid are targeting-cell and SOF learning; governance-without-disarmament remains the quarterly stabilisation case. No weekly trigger unless the ISF lands.

items.name: US–Israel–Iran

phase.now: Blockade and tanker war; MOU expired
phase.prev: Post-war MOU under a fragile stand-down

items.whyNow: Hormuz transits are at roughly 8 a day against a pre-war ~85, the US blockade and 'tanker-for-tanker' strikes are live, the MOU expired without extension, and Iran is widening coercion through IRGC-run Iraqi cells and Houthi chokepoint control. Highest Singapore-exposure item on the list.
changes: The 60-day MOU expired on 17 Aug with no extension after a July kinetic re-escalation (Iran struck shipping, closed Hormuz and hit US bases in five states) and a two-week exchange; Iran's 'few weeks' ultimatum has lapsed without a new date.

Kinetic resumption from 30 Aug: CENTCOM strikes on IRGC rocket and mine launchers on Larak Island days after declaring lanes mine-free; IRGC ballistic salvos on US bases in Jordan; after an IRGC missile salvo at a US carrier group, US strikes on IRGC-linked crude carriers (Downy, Stark 1, Kylo — 'tanker for tanker', 5–8 Sep).

Iran proposed an Oman-based Hormuz toll and management arrangement (IRGC claims revenue-share, 26 Aug) against Gulf pushback; transits ~8 a day on 13 Sep versus ~85 pre-war; the US blockade has redirected 110 ships; mine and debris risk persists (LPG carrier hit 21 Sep).

Iran shifted to multi-axis coercion as its coastal sensors degraded: lean IRGC-directed Iraqi cells (drones from Maysan shut the Saudi East-West pipeline 11–12 Sep) and Houthi coastal gains around Bab al-Mandab.
Witkoff held lengthy indirect talks with Araghchi at UNGA on 22 Sep; Trump says a settlement 'is going to be reached' but signalled it would likely follow the November midterms.

next.text: Iranian delegation in New York to 27 Sep meeting the mediators (Pakistan, Qatar, Oman, Turkey) after Pezeshkian's UNGA address.
next.ifSeen: An agreed channel or interim transit terms → CSI Flash the same day.

next.text: Daily Hormuz transits recover toward the ~85 baseline, or escorted convoys begin; Iran's reopening conditions (lift blockade, release assets, end operations on all fronts) met or dropped.
next.ifSeen: Downgrade Singapore exposure to Moderate; CSI action to weekly.

next.text: Another strike on merchant shipping or a US warship, a mine strike, or a strike on Gulf energy infrastructure after the tanker exchanges.
next.ifSeen: CSI Flash the same day; tempo and escalation stay at the ceiling.

next.text: A formal Iran–Oman Hormuz management arrangement with fees, or Gulf states' commitments to bypass routes.
next.ifSeen: Structural change to transit terms → CSI Flash; note for the quarterly.

next.text: US midterm elections — Trump's stated window for a settlement.
next.ifSeen: Post-election deal push → re-check phase weekly.

csi.rationale: Hormuz terms bear directly on Singapore fuel and shipping exposure; shadow-fleet tankers as kinetic nodes and the IRGC's lean Iraqi cells feed the monthly pattern review.

items.name: Israel–Lebanon

phase.now: Active enforcement: ridge cleared, pilot-zone handover stalled

items.whyNow: A months-long siege and the industrial demolition of the Ali al-Taher complex (about 1,100 tonnes of explosives, a magnitude 4.1 tremor), then the fight to hold the security zone against re-infiltration; the diplomatic track is frozen until after the 27 Oct Israeli election.
changes: First pilot-zone handover: LAF deployed into Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh on 21 Jul; Froun and Srifa still pending; mid-Aug ceasefire breakdown and decapitation strikes; the Rome round slipped from 1 Sep to 'October', with ambassadors meeting at the State Department in mid-Sep instead.

IDF declared operational control of the Ali al-Taher ridge (3 Sep) after weeks of siege, then demolished the tunnel and command complex on 10 Sep (~1,100 t of explosives, USGS magnitude 4.1); Hezbollah answered with one-way attack drones (26 Aug) and IEDs against consolidating engineer units.

A 'Gray Line' plan was reported (7 Sep): IDF pullback to 2–4 km inside Lebanon with ~20 permanent outposts, conditional on LAF control, disarmament commitments and a monitoring mechanism — not yet approved by Israel's political leadership.
Hezbollah rejects the disarmament terms and Iran calls the ground moves a major violation of the Islamabad agreement; no Military Coordination Group meeting has been reported since May.

next.text: Rome political round resumes (October, date not published), with the military track reportedly split to a CENTCOM venue in Florida.
next.ifSeen: Dated Froun/Srifa handovers → Weekly awareness post.

next.text: Israeli Knesset election; substantive withdrawal and pilot-zone talks expected only after the result (confirmed 4 Nov).
next.ifSeen: Re-check the Gray Line decision and CSI action after the result.

next.text: CENTCOM certifies the Froun and Srifa pilot zones and the IDF exits them.
next.ifSeen: Framework working → tempo down; Monthly pattern review on handover mechanics.

next.text: Israeli political approval of the Gray Line pullback and outpost plan.
next.ifSeen: Phase change to managed buffer → Weekly awareness post.

next.text: A Hezbollah re-infiltration attack causing IDF casualties inside the security zone, or an IDF strike inside a designated pilot zone.
next.ifSeen: Framework at risk → Weekly awareness post; CSI Flash if the LAF withdraws.

next.text: Composition and first meeting of the Military Coordination Group for Lebanon.
next.ifSeen: Scope what a regional-partner contribution would require; brief up.

csi.rationale: Subterranean denial as two tracks (tactical clearing, then strategic demolition) and persistent multi-spectrum ISR over a contested buffer are combat-engineer and intelligence learning; the MCG question stays time-sensitive for planners.

items.name: Thailand–Cambodia

phase.now: Physical hardening under a holding ceasefire; conciliation under way

items.whyNow: Thailand's publicly disclosed Falcon Team drone strikes on Cambodian counter-drone, EW and communications nodes near Preah Vihear are the first admitted cross-border UAS employment since the ceasefire, while the UNCLOS conciliation commission opened in Singapore (14–16 Sep).
changes: UNCLOS Annex V Conciliation Commission held its first meeting in Singapore, 14–16 Sep: terms of appointment and rules signed, ~12-month non-binding process; scope disputed (Thailand: delimitation only; Cambodia: a treaty including revenue-sharing).

Thai barrier phase 1 (1.3 km, Chanthaburi) complete and phase 2 (~7–8 km, markers 54–58) under way with access roads and bunkers; Cambodia lodged its strongest protests over PM Anutin's 23 Aug Hill 500 visit and a 3 Sep helicopter incursion; Thailand escorted ASEAN observers and media into O'Smach.

Thailand disclosed Falcon Team drone strikes on alleged Cambodian counter-drone, EW, communications and field positions around Preah Vihear (week of 14–21 Sep); Cambodia denies military use of the site; claims not independently verified. Tempo raised to Medium, adaptation to High.
39 Chinese T-59D tanks delivered in July (of 93 ordered); Thai NSC reports none near the border; GBC met 4–7 Aug in Malaysia, the JBC date remains unresolved; the land border stays largely closed.

next.text: Next Conciliation Commission meeting (dates not yet published) and any written pleadings schedule.
next.ifSeen: Scope agreed → legal track absorbs the dispute; scope fight → note for the monthly.

next.text: General Border Committee follow-up (promised 'in September') or a Joint Boundary Commission date.
next.ifSeen: Political track revived → tempo check; if neither convenes by November, escalation risk up.

next.text: 49th ASEAN Summit, Manila (published dates conflict: 10–12 or 16–18 Nov) — sideline trilateral as at the May summit.
next.ifSeen: Leaders' commitment on the JBC → Dashboard only; absence → Weekly awareness post.

next.text: Cambodian retaliation for the drone strikes, a landmine casualty, or an exchange of fire along the barrier line.
next.ifSeen: Move to Priority; CSI Flash.

next.text: Second Chinese tank batch lands, or tanks move toward the border sectors.
next.ifSeen: Grey-zone capability building → Monthly pattern review.

csi.rationale: Near-abroad and the first admitted cross-border UAS strikes: one awareness line this week; engineering consolidation and the access-and-verification information contest stay in the monthly pattern set.

items.name: US–Venezuela

phase.now: Managed transition on a US economic-first track; counter-cartel maritime campaign

items.whyNow: Tempo is up: a rebranded Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere strike campaign (70th boat strike on 19 Sep), the first government–opposition talks, 100-year oil concessions and a Trump–Rodríguez meeting at UNGA — with elections deferred and Machado's return attempts failing.
changes: 4 Aug: SOUTHCOM stood up Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere (18-nation Americas Counter Cartel Coalition), replacing Operation Southern Spear; 70th strike on 19 Sep (~234 killed to date, 14 strikes 23 Aug–19 Sep) with a late-August shift toward boarding before destruction; UN Special Rapporteur (22 Sep) calls the strikes serial extrajudicial killings.

First in-person government–opposition talks (6–14 Aug; second round 15–17 Sep): frozen assets for earthquake recovery and a Supreme Tribunal overhaul agreed; no election date — Rodríguez: 'when Venezuela is ready'; Rubio: 'not years, but months and weeks'.
28 Aug NABEP oil deal (100-year concessions on 17 fields, Pentagon 35% stake, $100bn pledged); Trump lifted the narco-state designation in mid-Sep; Chevron doubling output; TotalEnergies MoU 20 Sep.

22 Sep Trump–Rodríguez pull-aside at UNGA (first since Maduro's capture); the same day Machado made three failed return attempts by sea and air; protests up 181% year on year, 344 political prisoners, colectivos not dismantled (UN fact-finding mission, 16 Sep).

next.text: An election-date announcement, or Machado's return 'in coming weeks'.
next.ifSeen: Return without a date → unrest indicator; a date → consider moving to Watch.

next.text: Third round of government–opposition talks (political guarantees, prisoners, judiciary).
next.ifSeen: Transition consolidating → Monthly pattern review only.

next.text: Inter-American Development Bank board decision on the $2.5bn Venezuela loan (board pushback, date soft).
next.ifSeen: Economic-first track funded → transition stability up.

next.text: JTF-WHEM strikes extended to Mexico, Colombia or Cuba, or a Cuba fuel blockade.
next.ifSeen: Regional escalation → Weekly awareness post.

next.text: Carrier or amphibious-group reinforcement or drawdown in the Caribbean (USNI tracker).
next.ifSeen: Posture change → re-check escalation risk.

csi.rationale: Coalition counter-cartel maritime interdiction and post-intervention transition are pattern-review cases; no Singapore nexus and no weekly trigger.

items.name: South China Sea

phase.now: Physical-contact coercion at three features; PLAN layered behind the CCG

items.whyNow: Moved up to Priority: a Philippine marine injured at Second Thomas (20 Jul), radar locks and flares on Philippine aircraft (2 and 7 Sep), the 18 Sep ramming off Palawan, and a PLAN surface action group plus H-6K bombers now routinely at Scarborough — with the Code of Conduct's 2026 deadline landing at the Manila summit in November.
changes: 20 Jul: CCG small-boat ramming and melee at Second Thomas Shoal injured a Philippine marine; 23–24 Jul water cannon at Scarborough with a CNN crew aboard; the 22–23 Aug resupply ran under a 'provisional understanding' with notification.

Early Aug: PLA Southern Theatre surged a Type 052D, a Type 071 and frigates plus H-6K bombers with YJ-12 to Scarborough; 2 Sep 'Combat Patrol–Huangyan Dao' with JL-10 armed trainers locking radar on three Philippine aircraft; 7 Sep flares fired at a coast guard aircraft from Subi and Mischief reefs; a PLAN group (DDG, two 054A, 056A) now on station.
18 Sep: CCG-21585 rammed the fisheries vessel BRP Datu Magat Salamat 54 nm off Palawan during a fuel-subsidy run; the US ambassador condemned a 'deliberate ramming'.

Code of Conduct: China–ASEAN foreign ministers (22 Jul) reaffirmed the 2026 goal and the 58th joint working group met in Manila on 11 Sep, but Crisis Group assesses the optimism has 'largely evaporated'; a 14-nation statement marked the 2016 award's tenth anniversary; ADMM-Plus maritime exercise launched 20 Sep (USS Canberra, P-8A).

next.text: Trump–Xi summit in Washington — South China Sea language and any restraint understanding.
next.ifSeen: Explicit restraint → tempo may dip; silence → pattern continues.

next.text: Exercise Sama Sama (2025 ran 6–17 Oct; 2026 dates not yet published).
next.ifSeen: PLAN shadowing or radio challenges → note for the weekly.

next.text: Next Second Thomas Shoal resupply (roughly monthly; last 22–23 Aug).
next.ifSeen: Boarding or water cannon with injuries → CSI Flash.

next.text: 49th ASEAN Summit and ASEAN–China Summit, Manila (published dates conflict: 10–12 or 16–18 Nov) — the effective deadline for a '2026' Code of Conduct.
next.ifSeen: Diluted text or slippage → Weekly awareness post on ASEAN centrality.

next.text: Chinese boarding or seizure of a Philippine vessel, a Philippine fatality, direct PLAN (not CCG) action, or Manila invoking Mutual Defence Treaty consultations.
next.ifSeen: CSI Flash the same day.

csi.rationale: Incident cadence and the COC deadline make this a weekly item; grey-zone layering (armed trainers, radar locks, forward PLAN presence) goes to the monthly pattern set; a threshold event escalates to a Flash.

items.name: Taiwan Strait

phase.now: Quiet air, busy sea: CCG quarantine-style patrols east of Taiwan

items.whyNow: Singapore exposure raised: China Coast Guard 'law-enforcement' patrols east of Taiwan are now routine and a Singapore-flagged merchant ship complied with a CCG radio check. Han Kuang 42 ran unscripted with reservist brigades and drone logistics while US arms sales are frozen around Trump–Xi summitry.
changes: Late Jun–Jul: first and second CCG patrols 74–124 nm east of Taiwan radio-checking transiting merchantmen (a Singapore-flagged ship complied); Taiwan counted a record 110+ PLAN and CCG ships along the first island chain, while PLA air sorties fell ~52% year on year (Aug: 171 sorties, 55 median-line crossings) and no named drill was held.

Han Kuang 42 (5–14 Aug): ~5,000 reservists in two brigades, first M1A2T employment, a new Littoral Combat Command, a deliberate mobile-internet slowdown and urban-resilience drills with first drone logistics deliveries.

Budgets: 2027 defence budget NT$1.12 tn (3.01% of GDP, +18%); NT$607.6 bn supplementary (40,000 coastal attack drones, 600 reconnaissance drones, 100 USVs); Unmanned Vehicles Industry act; Kuma Academy civilian drone course selling out; reservist drone module under review.

US$14 bn arms package paused since May (Iran munitions); reports on 20–21 Sep that Washington is weighing a delay until after APEC and the G20 at Xi's request; New Zealand ships transited the Strait on 18 Sep.

next.text: Trump–Xi summit — any shift from 'does not support' to 'opposes' Taiwan independence, or an arms-sale freeze.
next.ifSeen: Wording shift → Weekly awareness post; arms freeze → note for the monthly.

next.text: Taiwan National Day address — a past trigger for PLA reactions.
next.ifSeen: Named PLA drill → escalation risk to High.

next.text: APEC Shenzhen — timing of US arms-sale decisions.
next.ifSeen: Package released or shelved → re-check state.

next.text: Taiwan local elections (KMT–TPP weighing referendums alongside).
next.ifSeen: Political trigger window for PLA activity.

next.text: CCG physically stopping or boarding a merchant ship east of Taiwan, or PLA sorties returning above 300 a month.
next.ifSeen: Move to Priority; CSI Flash on any Singapore-flagged vessel.

csi.rationale: Whole-of-society mobilisation (unscripted Han Kuang, comms-degradation drills, mass drone procurement, civilian drone literacy) is Army learning; the quarantine-rehearsal pattern is the quarterly candidate.

items.name: China–Japan

phase.now: Frozen diplomacy with EEZ live fire and expanding Nansei transits

items.whyNow: Moved up to Active: China–Russia live fire inside Japan's claimed EEZ (19 Jul), a JL-3 SLBM test into the Pacific, expanding PLAN transits of the Nansei passages and a record ¥8.9 tn budget request — while Beijing's precondition (revise the Taiwan position) leaves no de-escalation path.
changes: 26 Jun–2 Jul: eight PLAN ships used three of five Nansei passages alongside five Russian ships (MOD: 'expanding and intensifying'); 6 Jul JL-3 SLBM test ~7,000 km into the South Pacific (Pacific leaders' rebuke 4 Sep); 7 Jul JCG–CCG face-off in Senkaku territorial waters.

19 Jul: PLAN destroyer Kaifeng live-fired ~100 nm off Okinotori inside Japan's claimed EEZ beside a Russian corvette; Japan protested; Beijing: Okinotori 'is a rock'. No radar lock-on or unsafe intercept found since December 2025.

Diplomacy stays frozen ten months after PM Takaichi's Taiwan remark: seafood ban, travel advisory and rare-earth curbs in force (Chinese arrivals −57% in June); a cross-party Diet delegation (24–27 Aug) was told there is no policy change without a revised Taiwan position; Motegi–Wang 'exchange' in Manila disputed.

Japan: 2026 Defense White Paper names China the greatest strategic challenge; record FY2027 request ¥8.9 tn (AI, unmanned, stand-off, IAMD) with the three security documents to be revised by year-end; US–Japan–ROK trilateral and a Takaichi–Trump meeting (22 Sep) to pre-empt a US–China bargain. Singapore exposure raised to Moderate on rare-earth and supply-chain spillover.

items.name: India–Pakistan

phase.now: Frozen ceasefire; lawfare over the Indus Waters Treaty
phase.prev: Armed peace after the May 2025 exchange

items.whyNow: The Line of Control is quiet but the trigger set is live: Jaish-e-Mohammed infiltrators killed in Udhampur (16–17 Sep), Pakistan's 'act of war' line on water, India's rejection of the arbitration award on the Indus Waters Treaty, and both leaders at UNGA on 25 Sep.
changes: Indus Waters Treaty: the PCA Court of Arbitration ruled (31 Aug–1 Sep) that the treaty remains in force and 'abeyance' is impermissible, with interim restrictions on Ratle; India 'categorically rejects' the award as illegally constituted; Pakistan's corps commanders (8 Jul) called any diversion of its water share an act of war.

Targeting of non-locals returned to Kashmir (31 Jul Kulgam shooting, first since Pahalgam) with no Indian stand-off response; two JeM militants killed at Udhampur on 16–17 Sep with a high alert across Kathua–Kishtwar; 486 drones recovered on the Punjab border year to date; a Pakistani UAV tracked over Rajouri on 28 Aug.
Modi and Sharif co-attended the SCO summit (31 Aug–1 Sep) without a bilateral; Kartarpur remains closed; India's fourth S-400 regiment delivered in May, the fifth due in November.

Unverified (single source, CFR tracker): a reported 15 Sep collision between an Indian destroyer and a Pakistani patrol vessel in the Arabian Sea, and a 7 Aug Turkey–Saudi–Pakistan defence pact — confirm before use.

next.text: Sharif and Modi both address UNGA; watch Kashmir, water and terrorism rhetoric and rights of reply.

items.name: Myanmar civil war

phase.now: Dry-season offensives; resistance drone war on airpower

items.whyNow: Moved up to Active: a fibre-optic FPV strike on the Tada-U fighter base (10 Sep), the failed junta Operation 4926 in Rakhine and the Arakan Army's counter-offensive around Sittwe, 500+ air attacks a month, and an ASEAN seat decision at the November summit that Singapore is co-shaping.
changes: Air war intensifying: ACLED counts >450 civilian deaths in H1 2026 with a new 2–5-jet sustained-strike tactic; the NUG reports 530 aerial attacks and 139 civilians killed in August (Myaung monastery 21 Aug, Mindat 30 Aug, Shadaw 5 Sep).

Rakhine: junta 'Operation 4926' launched from the Sittwe, Kyaukphyu and Thandwe enclaves on 4 Sep (about 1,000 troops each, MLRS, drones, naval gunfire) and was repulsed by 5 Sep; the Arakan Army then took six or more outposts around Sittwe (15–19 Sep) and holds ~93% of the state; 5,000+ displaced.

Resistance drone warfare crossed a threshold: six fibre-optic FPV drones struck Tada-U airbase (Mandalay) on 10 Sep, the first strike on a fighter base; the KIA destroyed ~25 Irrawaddy supply vessels since late August and wiped out a 130-man Bhamo breakout column (12–14 Sep). Adaptation raised to High.

Politics: President Min Aung Hlaing's 100-day peace-talks deadline (31 Jul) passed with KNU, CNF and ABSDF rejection; state visits to China, Thailand and Vietnam; ASEAN (59th AMM, Manila) kept non-political representation and demanded 'demonstrable progress' — Singapore's foreign minister: 'not enough progress'; UN credentials contest ahead.

next.text: Post-monsoon offensives: junta pushes on Kanpetlet and Mindat (Chin), renewed Sittwe and Kyaukphyu breakouts, the KIA's Bhamo endgame (180-truck convoy into Saw on 19 Sep).
next.ifSeen: A major town changing hands → Weekly awareness post.

next.text: Further FPV strikes on airbases (Tada-U, Magway, Toungoo) and the junta's counter-UAS response (netting, dispersal).
next.ifSeen: Monthly pattern review on C-UAS for fixed bases.

next.text: 49th ASEAN Summit, Manila (published dates conflict: 10–12 or 16–18 Nov) — whether Min Aung Hlaing is seated (Thailand pushing; Manila, Jakarta, Kuala Lumpur and Singapore resisting).
next.ifSeen: Seat granted → ASEAN line breaks; Singapore exposure up.

next.text: UN Credentials Committee decision on Myanmar's representation (normally around November).

items.name: Other Middle East spillover

phase.now: Renewed Houthi–Saudi war; Houthi control of Bab al-Mandab; US exit from Iraq
phase.prev: Proxy pressure linked to the Iran track

items.whyNow: Moved up to Priority: the Houthis ended the 2022 truce, seized the full Red Sea coast including Perim and the Hanish islands (3–11 Sep), and cut Bab al-Mandab transits to ~12 a day; a Singapore-flagged VLCC has already diverted; Iraqi militia drones shut Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline while the US leaves Iraq by 30 Sep.
changes: Houthis declared the 2022 truce over and a 'naval blockade' of Saudi Arabia (20 Jul); ballistic missiles killed six on the Egyptian cargo ship Tihamah in Bab al-Mandab (11 Aug, first fatal ship attack since February) and hit a Bahri tanker off Yanbu (24 Aug); 12 attacks or attempts since July.

3–11 Sep offensive took Mocha, Hays, Khawkhah, the Hanish islands and Perim — the whole Red Sea coast; Lloyd's List transits fell from ~30 to ~12 a day, Brent above $100, Asia–Europe rates up 25–40%; Trump reportedly declined a Saudi request for air support; Saudi two-week ceasefire offer via Oman and US–Houthi talks in Muscat (18 Sep), no Houthi reply yet.

Iraq: PMF drones on Saudi oil (27–29 Jul) drew US–Saudi strikes on the PMF in seven provinces (29 Jul, 20+ killed); drones from Maysan shut the East-West pipeline (5m b/d) on 11–12 Sep; Patriots withdrawn from Erbil (5 Aug) and remaining US troops leave by 30 Sep, mostly to Jordan; Baghdad recast the 30 Sep militia disarmament deadline as the 'start of a process'.

Israel–Syria: 26 Jul incursion and checkpoint at Al-Ardah, eight strikes on Abu al-Duhur airbase (17–18 Aug, Turkish deployment cited), 267 violations in August; Jordan-hosted security talks (24 Aug) proposed a US-supervised operations room and Sharaa calls a deal 'progressing'; Katz: Israel will not leave Hermon or the buffer zone.

next.text: Houthi answer to the Saudi two-week ceasefire offer and the Muscat channel; whether non-Saudi hulls stay off the target list.
next.ifSeen: Acceptance → tempo down; a hit on a non-Saudi hull → CSI Flash on shipping-route exposure.

next.text: US-led coalition mission in Iraq ends; 1 Oct Iraq 'free of foreign military presence'; militia disarmament committee outputs.
next.ifSeen: Drone strikes on Erbil after Patriot removal → escalation indicator; KH/Nujaba refusal → note for the monthly.

next.text: Saudi East-West pipeline restart, or a second militia strike on Gulf energy infrastructure.
next.ifSeen: Energy-route exposure → CSI Flash.
